tools.name: get_framework_overview
tools.description: Returns the AI Capability Rollout Framework's three phases, four capability pillars, positioning, the recommended offer and the Discord community. Use it to explain what the framework is. It does not return prices or the FAQ. To check readiness, use assess_ai_readiness.

tools.name: get_pricing
tools.description: Returns current one-time prices and checkout links for the Framework + Executive Suite, the Framework alone, and AI at Work seats, including the seat tiers, co-branding and the Rollout Pack. Use it for the full price list, or get_seat_quote for a specific number of seats. It does not take payment. T

tools.name: get_faq
tools.description: Returns published questions and answers, optionally filtered by topic. Use it for specific questions about pricing, governance, implementation or the products. It does not search the long-form guides; use search_knowledge_base for that. To check readiness, use assess_ai_readiness.

tools.name: get_ai_at_work_course
tools.description: Returns the public outline of AI at Work, the employee AI training course: modules, what is included, seat tiers and the guarantee. Use it for questions about employee training. It does not return transcripts or quiz content. To check readiness, use assess_ai_readiness.

tools.name: search_knowledge_base
tools.description: Searches the framework's methodology, definitions, positioning and changelog for a phrase and returns matching sections with links to the source documents. Use it for a concept the other tools do not cover. It returns excerpts, not full documents. To check readiness, use assess_ai_readiness.

tools.name: assess_ai_readiness
tools.description: Runs the 16-question AI Readiness Score on the user's behalf (rate each statement 1-5, where 1 = Strongly Disagree and 5 = Strongly Agree) and returns their readiness stage, a recommended next step, and a link to the free full assessment on the site, which includes a personalized PDF. It returns no

tools.name: get_starter_kit
tools.description: Describes the free AI Capability Briefing Kit, a 10-page internal briefing document, and how to get it. Use it when the user wants a free starting resource. It does not deliver the file; use email_me_the_kit when the user asks for it by email. To check readiness, use assess_ai_readiness.

tools.name: get_seat_quote
tools.description: Calculates the AI at Work cost for a given number of seats (1-500), with optional co-branding. It flags when a higher tier is cheaper in total and shows the Executive Suite and Rollout Pack alternatives. It does not take an order. To check readiness, use assess_ai_readiness.

tools.name: email_me_the_kit
tools.description: Emails the free Briefing Kit to an address the user gives you. Call only when the user has explicitly asked to receive it by email and agreed to be emailed. Never call it on your own and never invent or guess an address. It adds the address to a mailing list and sends the kit by email.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_ai_at_work_course, get_starter_kit, email_me_the_kit · Private data: search_knowledge_base, get_starter_kit · Public sink: get_starter_kit, email_me_the_kit.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_ai_at_work_course, get_starter_kit, email_me_the_kit · Private data: search_knowledge_base, get_starter_kit · Public sink: get_starter_kit, email_me_the_kit

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
